newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan launches French frigate, tests US missile.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan launches French frigate, tests US missile.

text.p: Taiwan's military beefed up its combat power on Wednesday by commissioning the third of six French-made missile frigates and refitting 50 U.S. tanks.
The army also test-fired a new U.S.-made Patriot antimissile missile, a newspaper said.
Taiwan has said it must steadily upgrade its armed forces as relations with giant neighbour China remain tense.
Taiwan has ordered 200 Patriots from the United States, citing a need to counter China's growing missile arsenal.
The defence ministry declined to confirm or deny the China Times Express report of a Patriot test-firing.
Navy Commander-in-Chief Ku Chung-lien presided over the commissioning of the Lafayette-class frigate at the navy's Tsoying base in southern Kaohsiung.
"The commissioning of the Lafayette-class frigate serves to boost the defence capability of the second generation of our naval fleet," he said on state radio.

The so-called "stealth" warship, clad with radar-defying composite materials, was bought under a US$3 billion contract negotiated in the early 1990s before Paris bowed to Chinese pressure and agreed to stop arming Taiwan.
Army Chief of Staff Fo Shou-yeh told Reuters the military has a T$1.2 billion (US$40 million) budget to refit 50 M41-D tanks that the army has used for more than three decades.
The tank's firing power and radar detection system is being largely reinforced, he said.
Beijing, which has viewed Taiwan as a renegade province since a civil war split them in 1949, has threatened to retake the island by force if it declares independence.
